name: Digital Twin Development
title: Digital Twin Development | Connected Asset & Facility Views | Hitelecom
metaDescription: Custom digital twin development for industrial assets, buildings, warehouses and infrastructure. Connect asset models, monitoring data and maintenance workflows.
heroValue:
Operational context.
Connected to field data.
heroDescription: Bring equipment, spaces and monitoring records into a navigable digital representation. Hitelecom scopes custom asset models, 2D or 3D views, telemetry mapping and operator workflows around your facilities and data systems. View uploaded monitoring data online through an agreed Hitelecom Cloud integration or customer platform, and place configured threshold alarms in their equipment context. Model detail, data connections and acceptance are defined for the project.

featureTitle:
From model views.
To useful operations.
featureIntro: Build the digital context operators need: which asset is reporting, where it belongs, what changed, and which records support the next action. Start with a representative asset set before expanding the model.

features.title: Asset identities and relationships
features.text: Structure sites, buildings, systems, equipment and measurement points with stable identifiers. Record relationships such as located-in, supplies or monitored-by so a reading appears against the correct physical asset.

features.title: Purposeful 2D and 3D views
features.text: Select floor plans, equipment diagrams or a 3D model according to the task. Reuse licensed CAD/BIM/model inputs after reviewing geometry, conversion effort and navigation on the intended devices.

features.title: Measurements with provenance
features.text: Show the measured value, unit, timestamp and source identity together. Distinguish current, delayed, missing and invalid records instead of colouring an unreported asset as healthy.

features.title: Asset-level threshold context
features.text: Display received alarms beside the relevant room, component or equipment. Define limits, event priority, acknowledgement and notification integration around the agreed monitoring workflow.

features.title: Historical investigation
features.text: Scope time-range selection, synchronized trends and links between observations and recorded events. Specify retention and sampling semantics so operators understand gaps, aggregation and historical state.

features.title: Inspection and maintenance links
features.text: Connect selected assets to drawings, inspection photographs and maintenance records through agreed identifiers and permissions. Keep the source system responsible for its authoritative work-order record.

features.title: Role-based operating views
features.text: Define the sites, asset details and actions each user may access. Separate operator investigation, management summaries and engineering administration without exposing unrelated facility records.

features.title: Versioned integration and handover
features.text: Document model versions, point mappings, API contracts and deployment configuration. Agree source-code/model rights, third-party licences and maintenance responsibilities in the statement of work.

planningTitle:
Define the model.
Then define its use.
planningIntro: A useful digital twin brief separates the visual scene, the measured data and any calculation or simulation.

planning.title: Identify the operating questions
planning.text: List the decisions, users and information needed. Distinguish an operational visualisation from simulation, forecasting or control.

planning.title: Review models and source data
planning.text: Assess model formats, geometry, permissions and telemetry availability. Define missing-data and stale-data behaviour.
planning.brief: Model samples · Source API · Identifiers · Data quality

planning.title: Set acceptance conditions
planning.text: Agree representative datasets, interaction behaviour, supported devices and review scenarios before development.
planning.brief: Test data · Performance targets · User review · Handover

applicationsIntro: Explore specific workflows across twelve operating environments. Each example identifies project inputs, the proposed application output and an acceptance check. These are development scopes, not claims of completed customer deployments.

groups.title: Manufacturing plants and process equipment
groups.intro: Organise production assets by line, cell and utility system so operators can investigate conditions without losing equipment context.
groups.imageAlt: Process vessel, connected pipework and service access
groups.imageCaption: Representative application environment. Project scope and suitability are defined for the installation.

tasks.title: Production-line condition view
tasks.description: Navigate from a production line to the equipment and measurement points associated with an operating exception.
tasks.inputs: Line hierarchy, equipment tags and sample sensor records.
tasks.deliverables: Line-to-equipment drill-down with timestamped readings.
tasks.acceptance: A selected reading resolves to the agreed equipment tag.
tasks.considerations: Equipment state and maintenance state need separate definitions.

tasks.title: Shared utility relationships
tasks.description: Show which monitored compressors, pumps or utility branches supply the production areas represented in the model.
tasks.inputs: Utility drawings, asset relationships and available measurements.
tasks.deliverables: Supply relationships with linked condition trends.
tasks.acceptance: Selecting a utility identifies its documented downstream areas.
tasks.considerations: The relationship model is not a process simulation.

tasks.title: Maintenance investigation workspace
tasks.description: Bring the selected asset’s drawings, event history and inspection records into the same investigation path.
tasks.inputs: Asset register, document links and maintenance API samples.
tasks.deliverables: Asset record panel with authorized source links.
tasks.acceptance: Users open the correct record with their assigned permissions.
tasks.considerations: Work-order ownership remains with the nominated source system.

groups.title: Warehouses and automated storage
groups.intro: Relate rack rows, storage zones and handling equipment to the measurements and inspections assigned to each location.
groups.imageAlt: Warehouse aisle with shelving and stored goods
groups.imageCaption: Representative application environment. Project scope and suitability are defined for the installation.

tasks.title: Rack and aisle monitoring context
tasks.description: Locate the rack bay associated with a received tilt or vibration event and review its measurement history.
tasks.inputs: Rack map, bay IDs and available tilt/vibration records.
tasks.deliverables: Rack-to-point navigation with event and trend panels.
tasks.acceptance: A sample bay event highlights only the mapped bay.
tasks.considerations: Measured movement does not by itself establish structural safety.

tasks.title: Storage-zone environmental view
tasks.description: Present uploaded temperature and humidity readings within the correct storage rooms, aisles or defined zones.
tasks.inputs: Zone boundaries, sensor placements and environmental records.
tasks.deliverables: Zone views with source timestamps and trend links.
tasks.acceptance: Missing or stale points remain distinguishable from current values.
tasks.considerations: One sensor does not represent every location in a zone.

tasks.title: Handling-equipment inspection context
tasks.description: Associate conveyors, lifts or shuttles with inspection notes and received operating-state records.
tasks.inputs: Equipment hierarchy, inspection records and approved interfaces.
tasks.deliverables: Equipment drill-down and linked inspection evidence.
tasks.acceptance: A selected component opens its matching inspection record.
tasks.considerations: Machine command and safety functions require separate scope.

groups.title: Commercial buildings and campuses
groups.intro: Use a building-to-floor-to-room structure to put facility observations and service records in their spatial context.
groups.imageCaption: Representative application environment. Project scope and suitability are defined for the installation.

tasks.title: Room-level environmental investigation
tasks.description: Move from a floor view to the air-quality or temperature points serving a reported room condition.
tasks.inputs: Licensed floor plans, room IDs and sensor-to-room mapping.
tasks.deliverables: Room navigation with available environmental measurements.
tasks.acceptance: A selected room shows only its assigned measurement points.
tasks.considerations: Sensor exposure and room boundaries affect interpretation.

tasks.title: Plant-room equipment context
tasks.description: Connect HVAC and water-service equipment to the spaces they serve and their available condition records.
tasks.inputs: Plant schematics, equipment IDs and service relationships.
tasks.deliverables: Equipment-space relationships and condition panels.
tasks.acceptance: A known service relationship appears consistently across views.
tasks.considerations: Thermal or airflow simulation is a separate engineering task.

tasks.title: Facility service-record navigation
tasks.description: Let a facility team reach maintenance notes, manuals or inspection evidence from the relevant model object.
tasks.inputs: Asset document index and access-role requirements.
tasks.deliverables: Permission-controlled links from room and equipment objects.
tasks.acceptance: Unauthorized users cannot open restricted supporting records.
tasks.considerations: Document revision and ownership must be traceable.

tasks.title: Rack environmental exceptions

faqs.q: What will the first project deliver?
faqs.a: A defined asset structure, selected 2D or 3D views, mapped data connections and agreed operator interactions. The statement of work identifies the model detail, interfaces, test scenarios and handover items for the initial asset set.

faqs.q: Is this a visualization project or a physical simulation?
faqs.a: This service starts with connected asset representation and operational visualization. Physical simulation, state estimation, forecasting or diagnostic algorithms require separate models, suitable inputs and explicit validation.

faqs.q: Do we need a complete 3D model before starting?
faqs.a: No. A project can begin with licensed floor plans, equipment diagrams or a limited asset model. The appropriate detail follows the operating task; a complex model is useful only when its additional context serves that task.

faqs.q: Can existing BIM or CAD files be reused?
faqs.a: They can be reviewed for ownership, permitted reuse, format, geometry detail and conversion effort. The project should retain a mapping between model elements and operational asset identifiers after any conversion.

faqs.q: Can Hitelecom sensor data appear in the model?
faqs.a: An agreed Hitelecom Cloud or other receiving-system integration can provide uploaded monitoring records and configured threshold events. The scope defines available channels, identity mapping, timestamps, data quality and refresh behavior.

faqs.q: Can customer SCADA, BMS or maintenance systems be connected?
faqs.a: The interfaces can be assessed using sample APIs or data extracts and the customer’s access requirements. Protocol support, authentication, read/write boundaries and the responsible source system are defined per integration.

faqs.q: How are delayed or missing measurements shown?
faqs.a: The data contract defines source timestamps, quality flags and stale-data rules. The user interface should display these states explicitly rather than treating a missing update as a normal or safe condition.

faqs.q: Are threshold alarms generated inside the digital twin?
faqs.a: They may come from an existing monitoring platform or a separately scoped rules service. The project defines where thresholds are evaluated, how events reach the view and how notification or acknowledgement is handled.

Control is not part of the visualization scope by default. Any command path needs an explicit functional design, permissions, interlocks, operational responsibility and verification appropriate to the equipment.

Agree the representative model, asset count, data profile, target devices and interactions before development. Test those scenarios with the proposed deployment architecture instead of making a universal performance promise.

faqs.q: Who receives source code, models and deployment materials?
faqs.a: Source delivery, model ownership, reuse rights and deployment documentation are contractual items. Third-party models, libraries and services retain their licence terms; these should be identified before handover.

faqs.q: Why is there no product datasheet or fixed project price?
faqs.a: This is a custom software service. A statement of work, interface schedule, deliverables list and acceptance plan define the actual project; cost and timing follow review of that scope.
